_doc.what: TC proprietary veteran projection model v1: predicts NEXT-season PPR fantasy points per game from the season just played. Per-position Ridge regression — gradient boosting lost to Ridge at every position on the era-split test, so v1 is linear.
_doc.training: Feature seasons 2015-2024 -> target seasons 2016-2025; nflverse weekly stats + ffopportunity expected points (XFP). Row = player-season with >=1 game; target filtered to next_g>=6. Trained on the full history after the recipe was validated era-split (train targets <=2022, test 2023-25).

feature_glossary.fpg: PPR fantasy points per game, season N
feature_glossary.fpg_2yr: GAMES-WEIGHTED blend of the last two seasons: (g_N*fpg_N + g_prev*fpg_prev)/(g_N+g_prev), fpg alone with no prior season. v1.1 change: a 17-game season out-votes an 8-game one whichever year it was, so injury-shortened seasons defer to healthy ones (validated: +0.004-0.008 test R2 at every position over the fixed 0.65/0.35 blend).
feature_glossary.fpoe_g: actual minus expected fantasy points per game (efficiency over opportunity)
feature_glossary.td_oe: ALL season TDs (pass+rush+rec) minus ALL expected TDs — TD luck; negative weight = regresses
feature_glossary.team_changed: 1 if next-season team differs from season-N modal team
feature_glossary.dest_vacated: share of the NEXT team's season-N opportunity (tgt+car) that departed the roster
feature_glossary.peak_fpg: QB ONLY (v1.2): career-best season PPR FPG (>=8 games) through the feature season. Proven elite peaks carry real information the two-year window forgets — an injury year does not erase a 22-FPG season. Era-split: QB test R2 0.370 -> 0.382, rank corr 0.659 -> 0.671. Peaks need DEEP history: trained on 1999+; the builder aggregates 2010+ which is uncensored for every active player. Tested and REJECTED at RB/WR/TE (no lift).
feature_glossary.env_plays: team offensive volume: (pass att + carries) per team game, season N (WR: own + destination + delta)
feature_glossary.env_pass: team pass rate: pass att / (pass att + carries), season N
feature_glossary.env_pts: team scoring environment: skill-position PPR points per team game, season N
feature_glossary.apy_cap_pct: RB + TE (v1.4): cap-relative average-per-year of the contract ACTIVE in the projection season (current OTC mirror: nflverse contracts historical_contracts.PARQUET — the .csv.gz twin died in 2022 and silently sabotaged the first test). Teams play who they pay. RB is the most robust feature since the games-weighted blend (+0.013/+0.027/+0.022 R2 on three different splits, rank corr 0.746->0.757); TE wins the two modern splits. WR looked good on the stale file and REVERSED on current data — rejected. QB rejected (money too sticky to inform). Also rejected: contract-year flag, fresh-signing flag, rookie-draft-capital threat (negative everywhere).
feature_glossary.denv_plays: WR: env_plays of the DESTINATION team (equals own team when not moving)
feature_glossary.denv_pass: WR: env_pass of the destination team
feature_glossary.denv_pts: WR: env_pts of the destination team
feature_glossary.env_plays_d: WR: destination minus own env_plays — the volume change a mover walks into
feature_glossary.exp_td_g: expected total TDs per game (ffopportunity) — QB volume/quality of chances
feature_glossary.sos_pos: mean softness of the KNOWN next-season schedule vs my position: each opponent's prior-season PPR allowed/game to the position, z-scored within (season, position), averaged over the 17 opponents
feature_glossary.dest_aggr: destination team's NGS aggressiveness (tight-window throw rate), z within season — a decay marker; negative weight
feature_glossary.dest_pred_pts: destination team's PREDICTED next-season points_z (frozen team forecast: points+success+3rd-down)

_doc.scoring: score = intercept + sum(coef_i * (impute(x_i, median_i) - mean_i)/sd_i); clamp to [0, 30]. Pure math over this file — no sklearn at runtime.
_doc.tweak_workflow: Edit coefs here -> python build_seed.py (the tcproj block rescoring is cheap and cached) -> python bake_seed.py to preview. Coefs are in STANDARDIZED units: +1.0 means +1 predicted FPG per one standard deviation of that feature.
_doc.retrain: Research pipeline preserved in projections/tc_model_research/ (gitignored workspace — see its README). Rebuild the dataset, validate era-split with proj_eval.py, and only then re-freeze. Re-run after each completed season.
_doc.v1_1_note: v1.1 (2026-08-28): only change vs v1 is the games-weighted two-year blend. Candidates tested and REJECTED era-split: per-category td_oe fix, passing-TD-over-expected, rushing 1st downs, sack rate, elite-production hinge (QB hinge coefficient learned ~0 — the data would not ratify extra credit for the elite tail).
_doc.v1_2_note: v1.2 (2026-08-28): QB gains career peak FPG (the "his last full season was elite" signal — user-hypothesized, era-split-validated). Also tested from the same study and rejected: partial-game-robust FPG (no lift anywhere once peak is in), and tier x situation interaction terms (the cohort effect is real — elite RBs moving to volume teams gained +1.1 FPG while fringe movers lost -2.2 — but existing features already price it).
_doc.v1_3_note: v1.3 (2026-08-28): team-ENVIRONMENT features — the statistical shadow of scheme/coaching (volume, pass rate, scoring env; destination + deltas for movers). WR: full set, robust on three different era splits (+0.008/+0.013/+0.008 R2). QB: trimmed to own-team env_pts+env_pass (+0.020/+0.025 on the two modern-era splits, -0.007 on the thin pre-2020 split — the effect is a modern-offense phenomenon; revisit as seasons accrue). RB/TE tested and rejected (flat/negative). Also from the same study: position-specific vacated share (rejected), kitchen-sink GBM (still loses to Ridge at every position), and learning curves showing Ridge plateaus with training size while GBM trails even at 100% — the model is signal-limited at season grain, not model-class-limited.
_doc.v1_4_note: v1.4 (2026-08-28): RB and TE gain cap-relative contract APY (user-hypothesized "teams play who they pay" — the David Montgomery case). Lesson logged: the first validation ran on a stale contracts file (csv twin frozen at 2022 signings) and produced the OPPOSITE per-position verdict; always check asset freshness.
_doc.per_position_keys: Each of QB/RB/WR/TE holds: features (ordered list — position feature sets DIFFER: QB carries peak_fpg + own-team env, WR carries the full 9-feature env block, RB/TE carry apy_cap_pct), median (imputation for missing inputs), mean + sd (standardization), coef (STANDARDIZED Ridge weights — +1.0 means +1 projected FPG per one SD of that feature), intercept (the average next-season FPG of trained players at that position), n_train. score = intercept + sum(coef*(impute(x)-mean)/sd), clamped to [0,30].
_doc.rookie_note: ROOKIE block (2026-08-28): drafted players with no NFL tape get a TC number too — predicted ROOKIE-season PPR total / 17 ("per-slate": never-played draftees trained as zero, so bust risk is inside the number, matching the 17-game basis of Sleeper baselines). Features per position: log2(draft pick), draft age, and (where it beat pick+age era-split) the cfb prospect model's calibrated hit probability — the two models compose. Trained on draft classes 2016-2025; era split classes <=2021 vs 2022+.
_doc.v1_6_note: TD block fix (2026-09-04): QB td_oe was miscomputed — (rush+rec TDs) minus TOTAL expected TDs incl. passing made every QB ~-20 "unlucky"; the term was really a passing-volume proxy. QB now uses exp_td_g (expected total TDs/game — the honest form of that signal); skill spots keep td_oe computed as ALL TDs minus ALL expected TDs. Era-split on identical data: ties RB/WR/TE, improves QB (rho .669 vs .665). proj_eval.py section 7 now tracks signed ME / calibration slope / per-decile bias; the +0.5..+1.2 fpg test-era over-projection is era drift (train bias 0.00 everywhere), absorbed by the annual retrain.
_doc.v1_7_note: SOS as a projection input (2026-09-05): tested at all four positions; adopted at QB ONLY. RB/WR were honest nulls, TE was rejected on a backwards coefficient (confound), QB gained +0.009 R2 / +0.006 rho with the gain positive in each test year and residual corr +0.354. CAVEAT: the QB effect is much stronger post-2022 than in the training era (train residual corr +0.055) — an emerging signal; recheck at each annual retrain. Also studied and REJECTED the same day: coaching/playcaller features (career track record of the incoming OC/HC from Wikipedia staff history, change flags) — the track-record table itself is sound (Ben Johnson +1.52, Nagy +0.07 once his Bears years pool in) but adds nothing over the env_* features at any position: env already prices the offense, the name adds no player-level signal.

team_forecast.what: predicts a team's next-season points_z from ppg_z + success_rt_z + third_conv_z (all z within season); coefficients fit on ≤2020 targets and frozen with the recipe. Used to build dest_pred_pts at score time.

_doc.v1_8_note: The trait screen (2026-09-05): every team-level playcalling/efficiency stat the app tracks, screened describe/persist/LEAD against next-season scoreboard points, 2011-2025. Findings: success rate is the master leading trait (predicts next-year points better than points do); red-zone TD rate is luck (persist .09, lead -.05); motion is the stickiest identity (persist .71) but does not lead; NGS aggressiveness is the strongest decay marker (lead -.12, negative 8 of 9 seasons). Adopted: QB dest_aggr (destination aggressiveness z, coef negative) and RB dest_pred_pts (destination PREDICTED next-season scoring via the frozen team forecast — predicted beats realized env at RB, which had no environment features). Rejected with cause: pressure_rt (backwards sign, confounded), pace/sec_play (per-year sign flips), rz/explosive/epa_rush (symptoms, no lead), shotgun/no-huddle/scramble/motion (identities, no lead). Watchlist: RPO rate and 4th-down aggression (single-window leads), pace.
